title: Fusion stability probe: random-seq benchmarks and regression notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for an experiment probing fusion stability across mixed-length workloads. We saw intermittent tail spikes in production after enabling fused attention+proj kernels on the flash path. Objective is to reproduce, quantify, and produce mitigations (config knobs, kernel fallbacks) before enabling fusion by default on Dedicated clusters.

High-level hypothesis:
- Fusion reduces aggregate kernel overhead but introduces contention/ordering sensitivity across CUDA streams and the KV cache when inputs are variable length.
- Paged attention (explicit KV paging) changes memory pressure patterns; combined with fusion we may get transient fragmentation leading to large p99/p999 spikes.
- Non-deterministic stream scheduling can amplify small per-request variance into observable latency tail events.

Test matrix (what we ran):
- Model: Llama-2-13b-chat (fp16), standard KV cache layout
- Hardware: A100-40GB (nv=470), single-GPU worker
- Runtimes: runtime v0.9.3 (baseline, unfused kernels), runtime/opt/fusion-experiment branch (fused attention+proj kernels), and paged-attn toggle on/off 
- Workloads: 3 sequence-length mixes
  * mix A: uniform short (10 tokens, 2000 qps synthetic)
  * mix B: mixed (10/128/512 with probs 0.6/0.3/0.1)
  * mix C: heavy-long (512/1024 50/50)
- Batching: dynamic batching latency SLO 40ms target (batch timeout 8ms), max batch 64
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latency for first-token and total-response, GPU utilization, memory alloc/free rate, kernel call counts, stream sync events, CUDA meminfo snapshots, profiler traces (nsight timestamps), and CPU-side scheduling (thread contention).

Commands to reproduce (local harness):
# start worker (fusion branch)
python -m ri.worker --model llama2-13b --quant none --fusion-enabled true --paged-attn false --batch-timeout-ms 8 --max-batch 64

# run synthetic client (mix B)
python tools/synth_client.py --qps 2000 --mix "10:0.6,128:0.3,512:0.1" --duration 20m --collect-traces /tmp/run1

Quick results summary (observed):
- Baseline (no fusion): stable p99 ~ 95ms on mix B, p999 ~ 220ms occasional. GPU util 62-74%.
- Fusion-only (paged-attn=false): median latency down 12-15%, p95 down 8%, but p999 increased to ~480-1200ms depending on run; saw repeated 1–2s tail spikes ~every 3–5 minutes.
- Fusion + paged-attn=true: overall latency slightly higher than fusion-only for short requests (due to paging overhead), but tail spikes less frequent and lower magnitude (~350–700ms p999).
- Heavy-long (mix C): fusion gave throughput gains but increased memory alloc churn; paged-attn improved stability.

Trace-level observations:
- When tail spikes occur we saw a cluster of >10 small cudaFree/cudaMalloc ops in short succession (fragmentation pattern).
- Kernel timeline shows fused attention kernel execution times consistent, but additional small helper kernels (proj, bias-add, reorder) sometimes scheduled on the same stream and blocked waiting for an in-flight memcpy (host->device) that came from background KV page-in.
- NVTX traces show stream interleaving: fused kernel on stream 7, then small memcpy on stream 2 with implicit stream waits due to event recording; ordering dependency created a stall.
- CPU thread dump correlates with one worker-thread doing synchronous page-in while the batching thread is holding a mutex for batch assembly (rare).

Hypothesized root causes (ranked):
1) Paging interactions: paged-attn introduces host-device memcpys that are not fully async relative to fused kernel streams because of event placement; this causes head-of-line blocking.
2) Allocation fragmentation: fused kernels allocate temporaries with short lifetimes; paging increases peak allocations which leads to more frequent small allocations when memory is fragmented.
3) Stream scheduling nondeterminism: fused kernels reduce kernel count but increase per-kernel criticality; any small aux op that blocks a stream has amplified impact.

Mitigations tested and notes:
- Move KV page-ins to a dedicated stream and prefetch earlier: reduced frequency of large spikes by ~40% on mix B. Implementation: async page-in stream + cudaEvent timeline to ensure prefetch completes before request enters service. Caveat: increased peak memory footprint.
- Eager allocation pooling for fused-kernel temporaries: cut p999 by ~25% in several runs. We used a thread-local arena for scratch buffers.
- Fallback path: if page-in queue length > X, disable fusion for next N requests (trialed X=8, N=64). This yielded the most stable p999 but cost ~8% median regression. Good candidate for a rollout safety policy.
- Batch-assembly mutex relaxation: changed to reader-writer pattern to avoid holding mutex during page-in scheduling; marginal improvement.

Open experiments (next steps):
- Instrument kernel-level alloc/free sizes and map to request IDs (need to propagate request id through runtime).
- Run same tests on multi-GPU worker with NCCL to see if inter-GPU comms worsen or mask the effect.
- Evaluate enabling kernel fusion only for sequence lengths > 64 to avoid amplifying short-request variance.
- Try an alternate fusion strategy: split fused kernel into compute-heavy core (latency-critical) and post-processing kernel on separate stream so helper ops don't block the critical path.

Immediate recommendations for rollout policy (short-term):
- Do not enable fusion-by-default on Dedicated until we have fallback policy and prefetching in place.
- Implement a fusion-safety toggle driven by simple heuristics: current page-in backlog, recent p99 over 1 minute window; if thresholds exceed, switch to unfused kernels for a short cooldown period.
- Add allocation pooling for fused kernels and enable it behind a runtime flag.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Why do factory-default cudaMalloc/cudaFree patterns show more churn with fusion? Is it due to slightly different scratch sizes (alignment) when kernels merge?
- Need to check if the fused kernel is setting stream flags (non-blocking) properly; review the kernel-launch code generator.
- Are there differences in how fused ops use cublas/cuBLAS handles that could induce implicit stream sync?

fusion-only: p50 29ms, p95 110ms, p99 250ms, p999 740ms
fusion+paged: p50 31ms, p95 115ms, p99 230ms, p999 420ms
